brainlife.desc: Connectivity matrix: one or more CSV matrices between parcels, with index.json describing each CSV and label.json naming each row/column.
brainlife.name: neuro/conmat
brainlife.readme:
# `index.json`

`/csv` directory contains any number of .csv files. `index.json` is used to describe each .csv files. It looks like this

```
[
    {
        "filename": "correlation.csv",
        "unit": "xyz^3",
        "name": "corrleation between 2 parc",
        "desc": "edit me"
    }
]
```

# `label.json`

Describes what each column/row corresponds to (in the same order of the column/row in the correlation.csv). It hould look like this.

```
[
    {
        "name": "self-loop",
        "desc": "index(x,x) is the diagonal"
    },
    {
        "name": "lh.Background+FreeSurfer_Defined_Medial_Wall.label",
        "label": "1001",
        "voxel_value": 1
    },
    {
        "name": "lh.17Networks_LH_VisCent_Striate.label",
        "label": "1002",
        "voxel_value": 2
    },
    {
        "name": "lh.17Networks_LH_VisCent_ExStr.label",
        "label": "1003",
        "voxel_value": 3
    },
...
]
```

**Use for:** Network analysis of structural or functional connectomes. Converting to network graphs or computing connectivity predictors.

**Not for:** Comparing matrices built from different parcellations or edge weights. Interpreting without label.json, which defines the node order.

**BIDS:** no BIDS counterpart.

**Sharing:** Tier 2 (pseudonymised participant-level) by default.

**Apps:** Input to 4 Apps, output of 9 Apps.

Full record: https://github.com/brainlife/abcd-spec/blob/master/datatypes/neuro.conmat.json

Directory of square CSV connectivity matrices (e.g. count, density, correlation).

identifying_risks: Individual connectomes can re-identify a person across datasets (connectome fingerprinting)
governance.rationale: Tool 1 step 6: participant-level derivative; step 7 moves fingerprint use to Tier 4.
sharing_cautions: Do not link matrices to behavioural or clinical data outside the governed project
tier_conditions: Tier 4 when used or released as connectome fingerprints or to predict traits or behaviour
Tier 1 when averaged across enough participants that no individual can be singled out
